jobs.title: Senior UX/Service Designer in Oda Systems
jobs.description:
The opportunity

You'll design the tools that get groceries onto millions of doorsteps: not what shoppers see, but the systems used by people working in logistics operations at our fulfillment centers.

Oda’s mission is to build the world’s most efficient retail system so people have space for life. A huge part of that is our sophisticated fulfillment and delivery system, designed and built entirely by us. It packs and delivers nearly a half million items every day to around 80.000 homes and businesses across Norway and Sweden. What we’ve built is second-to-none in the world when it comes to efficiency, and it’s held together by internal tools and processes that make the jobs of operators and drivers easy, fast, ergonomic, and smooth. That's where you come in.

You'll work in close collaboration with our colleagues in both Norway and at our sister company Mathem in Stockholm, and you’ll help us on the path to launching Oda Systems in new markets as we find customers who want to work with us to continue building the most efficient solution for online groceries.


The role

Service/UX designers play a major part in the design of our processes and tooling. Great processes are as much about ergonomics, workflow, physical space, team structures, and incentives as they are about screens. You’ll get the chance to not only work on software solutions but also consider how digital experiences should best interact with hardware/machinery, the physical space they’re situated in, and last but not least the operator routines around them. That combination is what makes logistics design at Oda different from most UX roles: you're never just designing a screen, you're designing a multi-dimensional workflow.

You'll join the Sourcing team within Oda's Logistics platform, designing the best possible experience for employees working with everything from receiving and restocking products to handling fruit & vegetables and our bakery tools. While we’re happy with today’s processes, we’re not satisfied: there is a ton to be done to make things more efficient, more automated, and smarter, so that we have even better control over inventory, workers have an easier workday, customers get fresher food, and we have even less product spoilage.

You'll work in a cross-functional team, closely collaborating with other disciplines – Product Management, Engineering, Data and Insight, and Logistics development. This is a hands-on, office-based role. You'll be at our Fulfillment Center in Lier regularly, and at our Tøyen office most of the week (most of the team is at Tøyen at least 3 days a week).


What you'll do in Oda

  • Lead big projects from start to finish: own them from the initial idea through concept, design, prototyping, implementation, testing, and follow-up after launch, working closely with the Sourcing team, and stakeholders in Logistics. You should feel comfortable taking on complex, large projects that require collaboration across teams.

  • Conduct UX research: observe what’s going on in operations, run workshops with your team, stakeholders, and our end-users in logistics operations.

  • Communicate and present your work to peers as well as stakeholders, showing your process, and the impact of your designs.

  • Map and model complex, systemic workflows.

  • Design user interfaces and build prototypes. You don’t have to be a pixel perfectionist, but you will draw screens. Prototype in Figma, or directly in code – whatever’s the fastest way to test an idea, with room to ship and test changes in production alongside developers.

  • Work closely with teammates and stakeholders all the way from ideation to roll-out, rather than handing off at the end of a solo-design process.

  • Raise the bar for design in your team and help shape how we approach logistics problems more broadly.


What we're looking for 🌟

  • At least 8 years of experience in UX, interaction, or service design, in-house or agency, with a portfolio showing full ownership from insight to shipped product

  • A full-stack design attitude: insight, concept, structure, and visual design, without waiting for handovers. Being open to being hands-on both on the warehouse floor and in our codebase.

  • Very solid fundamentals in product sense and design: demonstrated insight-centric process, root cause analysis, work framed in desired outcomes, ability to distill complexity.

  • Speed over perfection: You understand the importance of shipping fast, learning, and iterating over polishing a "perfect" blueprint. You leverage the advantage we have with having short feedback loops with our end-users.

  • A track record of driving process change: not just shipping a solution, but bringing the operators who'll use it along with you.

  • You already use AI as part of your own design process: you're genuinely interested in an AI-enhanced product development workflow, not just AI features bolted onto Figma.

  • Fluent English. Intermediate Norwegian or Swedish is a strong plus, since you'll be working directly with warehouse operators on-site.

  • Previous logistics experience is a plus, not a requirement.


What we offer 🚀

  • A flexible schedule built around a healthy work-life balance.

  • Modern, empowered product teams: democratized data access, good tools, a sustainable pace. We ship, and you will immediately see the impact of your work.

  • A team that's actively working AI into both design and development, not just talking about it, and genuinely open to designers who want to prototype or write code.

  • A design community across all Oda teams: UX design, Service design, Digital design, UX research, Content design, and Graphic design.

  • A culture that values kindness, transparency, and taking action over process for its own sake.

  • A modern office at Tøyen with an amazing subsidized canteen by Naked Lunch, bike parking, and a great rooftop terrace.

You'll be working with people who are ambitious about logistics in a way most designers never get to be. Come build the future with us.


Oda is committed to being an inclusive community, cultivating diversity, equity, and belonging into our everyday workplace culture. When hiring for our team, we welcome the unique contributions that people can add with different cultural backgrounds, ethnicity, race, gender, gender identity and expression, nationality, age, languages spoken, color, religion, disability, sexual orientation, education and beliefs. If you have a disability such as a hearing, visual impairment or any other neurodivergent need that requires accommodating during the hiring process, please let us know in advance. You can do this by contacting the job owner or hiring manager.

Please apply by 20th of September.

We look forward to hearing from you! 💛

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Oda is the leading online grocery retailer in Norway, but as a company, we’re first and foremost an ambitious tech and logistics company - not a classic retailer. We’re one of the fastest-growing startups in the Nordics, working with huge, complex challenges to make the lives of our customers simpler and easier. Want to join us? Our goal is to create the world's most efficient retail system. Through smart work, passionate customer focus and our own technology we make a difference in the lives of thousands of customers and change society for the better through a completely re-imagined value chain for grocery shopping. Our customers save more than 60 hours a year, time we believe can be better spent than going to the store. Our effective value chain and logistics save society tonnes of food waste each year and our distribution network replace almost 13,000 individual trips by car to the grocery store each year.

jobs.title: Senior Fullstack Software Engineer
jobs.description:
About Falkor

We build industrial intelligence software for heavy-asset sectors. As a KONGSBERG company backed by over 200 years of heritage, Falkor helps the energy, chemicals, utilities and other industrial sectors operate with absolute clarity, confidence, and control.

Our AI-enabled platform connects people, systems, and workflows—expanding human capability by turning complex data into real-time, actionable decisions. We help leading organizations improve safety, efficiency and performance while redefining how heavy assets are designed and operated.


The role

We are looking for a Senior Fullstack Software Engineer to help design, build, and continuously improve Falkor Horizon and the platform capabilities it depends on. In this role, you will contribute across frontend and backend, take ownership of features from idea to production, and help the team deliver reliable, intuitive, and scalable solutions. We are looking for a flexible, hands-on engineer who can get up to speed quickly and contribute where the team needs it most.


What You’ll Do

  • Build and improve end-to-end product features across frontend and backend.

  • Develop intuitive web experiences and scalable backend services, APIs, integrations, and data flows.

  • Own features through design, implementation, testing, release, and observability.

  • Contribute to architecture, reliability, security, scalability, and performance.

  • Work closely with Product, UX, Platform, Data, and DevOps colleagues to turn user and business needs into working software.


What we're looking for

  • 6+ years of professional software development experience, with strong hands-on experience across both frontend and backend.

  • Strong experience with TypeScript/JavaScript, Node.js, and a modern frontend framework, preferably Angular.

  • Good understanding of API design, object-oriented programming, system design, and service-oriented architecture.

  • Experience with distributed systems, databases, caching, messaging, and cloud-native architecture.

  • Hands-on experience with automated testing, debugging, observability, and CI/CD for production services and web applications.

  • Experience with one or more relevant data technologies, such as MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Redis, Elasticsearch, InfluxDB or TimescaleDB.


Nice to Have

  • Experience building complex web applications, design systems, data visualization, or workflow-oriented user interfaces.

  • Experience with microservices, event-driven architecture, Docker, Kubernetes, and Azure or AWS.

  • Experience with authentication, authorization, security best practices, and resilient production-grade services.

  • Experience with industrial software, digital twins, data platforms, analytics, or GenAI/LLM-enabled product capabilities.


Why join Falkor?

You'll be joining a global technology company helping to redefine how complex industries operate.

At Falkor, you'll have the opportunity to:

  • Work on meaningful challenges with real-world impact

  • Collaborate with talented colleagues across technology and industry domains

  • Learn from experts in software, engineering, operations, and digital transformation

  • Grow your career in a business that is expanding globally

  • Help shape technology that expands human capability in complex industries

We believe diverse perspectives make us stronger and are committed to creating an environment where everyone feels respected, included, and able to do their best work.


Ready to apply?

If you're excited about solving complex challenges and making an impact through technology, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today with your resume.


Agency notice

Falkor occasionally partners with selected recruitment agencies for specific hiring requirements. We do not accept unsolicited candidate submissions and will not be responsible for associated fees unless terms have been agreed in advance through our Procurement team.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

At Kongsberg Digital, our mission is to transform the world’s most complex and asset-intensive industries through world-leading, AI-powered digital twin technology. As a pioneer in industrial digitalization, we provide a comprehensive suite of software solutions that empower organizations to manage the full lifecycle of their assets—more efficiently, safely, and sustainably than ever before. The industry is on the cusp of a digital revolution—and we’re leading the charge. From early adoption of AI to building trusted partnerships with some of the world’s largest industrial players, we are redefining how work gets done. With domain expertise baked into every line of code and a high-calibre team united by a clear mission, we’re not just keeping pace with change—we’re setting the standard. As we expand rapidly across the Middle East and Africa, deepen our end-to-end offerings, and push the boundaries of AI, now is the perfect time to join a company that’s growing fast, thinking bold, and delivering real impact.

jobs.title: AI Integration Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us

At No Isolation, we’re a profitable, 65-person Scandinavian EdTech scale-up operating across Europe. We help educators bring learning and belonging to every child.

Our AV1 robot is deployed in 19 countries, with 5,000+ units supporting schools to improve attendance, belonging, and continuity of learning for children who cannot be physically present. Consistently described as life-changing, it bridges the gap between the student and their peers, restoring both educational continuity and the essential sense of social belonging.

We’re established enough to have a proven solution and strong financial foundations, yet still small enough for every new colleague to have a visible impact on our next stage of growth.

The Opportunity — AI Integration Engineer

This is a new role at No Isolation, and you'd be the first person in it.

You'll sit inside Engineering but work mostly embedded inside selected internal business units, in contrast to the rest of Engineering. You’ll work with Sales, Customer Success, Finance and Operations. You’ll connect the tools they depend on and implement AI tools and automation flows to positively impact our revenue first and foremost, but also generally enhance internal effectiveness.

In practice: you set the bar for how much internal AI and Automation can change the company from the inside in 2026 and beyond, and you co-own the stack you put in place. You will have a lot of direct contact with the teams you're building for, and a lot of say in how the technical side gets structured to enable you, while having the support of experienced software engineers when needed.

What You'll Do — Scope & Responsibilities

  • Systems integration: Drive automation of key business areas and connect our business tools across Data, IAM, CRM, ERP (Odoo) and Finance through APIs, webhooks and events, so data stays in sync across systems.

  • Internal automation capability: Build and maintain workflows in Windmill and/or n8n; migrate us off legacy SaaS and iPaaS tools as you go. Aim to articulate as many problems as possible as deterministic automations that keep data and AI cost low.

  • Internal AI capability: Contribute to shared infrastructure for using AI internally alongside our cloud/platform engineers: assistants, retrieval over internal knowledge, summarisation, classification, routing, etc. Turn ad hoc AI experiments into tools people can actually rely on, with eval sets in place to catch regressions.

  • Data & internal foundations: Centralise data into sources the business can trust, reconcile figures across systems so numbers match wherever they appear, and provide internal tools and lightly-built apps.

  • Guardrails & cost control: Define the standards for how integrations and AI get built here. Keep the set of automation platforms small and deliberate (e.g. Windmill, n8n and some custom). Track AI spend and return on investment so we can monitor alignment between the two.

  • Partnership: Work directly with the teams you're building for: understand the actual problem, ship a working increment near-instantly, then iterate and negotiate toward durability. You're measured on time saved, additional revenue generated, budget synergies realised, not on the tools you ship. Share knowledge and lift others through e.g. workshops and townhalls.

What You Bring — Experience & Capabilities

  • Talent for working directly with non-technical stakeholders and turning a fuzzy request into a concrete system. This is a first-of-its-kind role here, so you're setting direction rather than following an existing playbook.

  • Experience connecting systems through APIs, webhooks and events: ERPs (Odoo v18 and beyond is a plus), CRMs, or Finance systems. At ease with various application protocols (REST), auth flows (OAuth/SSO) and the rough edges of third-party SaaS APIs.

  • Hands-on with a code-first orchestration platform: Windmill, Temporal, Airflow, n8n or similar.

  • A builder who finishes: Proficient in at least one general-purpose language (Python, TypeScript, Go), and comfortable taking something from rough prototype (built by you or non-technical people) to engineering standard.

  • Comfortable using and configuring self-hosted tooling (containers, secrets, backups, upgrades) to some extent, as opposed to fully leaning on managed SaaS

  • Practical experience with LLMs and agents: context engineering, RAG, evals, tool/function calling. You should have a good sense of where AI helps and where it adds fragility.

  • Data sense: savvy with SQL and common data stores; able to model, reconcile and centralize data; some exposure to classical machine learning can be an advantage.

  • Security-conscious by default: least-privilege access, careful handling of secrets, aware of GDPR, SOC and ISO requirements.

  • STEM degree (BSc/MSc) or equivalent practical experience in integration, AI & automation, or internal tooling.

  • Experience at product or scale-up companies is an advantage.

Why You'll Love It Here

  • First-of-its-kind role: you will tackle opportunities unexplored so far at the company

  • Purpose with scale: The systems you build free up time that goes straight back into helping educators support thousands of children connected, learning, and included every single day.

  • Work with exceptional leaders: You'll report to our Director of Engineering, Jerome, with plenty of room to shape a high-trust, learning-driven engineering culture.

  • Growth through ownership: A lean environment with the freedom to propose what you think is best for our very company.

  • Stability with a lean size: We are profitable and growing rapidly, while keeping at a size where the ideal candidate will have high impact.

  • Flexible working around core hours (10:00–15:00), with a hybrid work schedule.

  • 27 vacation days.

  • Travel and accident insurance for you and your immediate family.

  • Enhanced parental and sick leave.

  • Mobile phone and internet subscription reimbursement.

  • Regular company socials and an annual trip away together.

Our Tech Stack

Think internal tools, fleets of connected robots, and the systems that keep Sales, Finance and Customer Success running. You'll work with:

  • Orchestration & automation: Windmill, n8n

  • Languages: Go, Python, TypeScript

  • Systems: Odoo, HubSpot, and the wider CRM/finance/IAM stack

  • AI: LLMs and agents, RAG/retrieval, MCP, evaluation tooling

  • Infrastructure: AWS, Kubernetes, containers

  • Data: SQL, MySQL, ClickHouse

  • Development: GitLab, Claude Code and handful of other solutions being evaluated

Location

This role is based in Oslo with hybrid flexibility at our headquarters (up to 2 days remote work per week).

We welcome all qualified applicants. Due to current visa/work-permit processes, we can progress candidates already in Norway or relocating with no need for additional work permit (such as the EU/EEA citizens). (This note is about work authorization only; no sensitive personal data is required).

How to Apply

If you like building things that make everyone else's work easier, are passionate about AI, and want that to matter for something bigger, we'd love to hear from you.

Please click Apply and upload your CV in English.

If you'd like, you can also include a short video as part of your application — this is optional, but it gives us a chance to see a bit more of who you are beyond your CV.

🎥 You may watch how AV1 transforms inclusion in education here: vimeo.com/1098745115

🌍 You may explore our mission and impact stories at noisolation.com

We kindly ask external recruitment agencies to refrain from contacting us regarding this position.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

We help educators bring learning and belonging to every child. School absence is the biggest challenge facing education. Our AV1 robots connect absent students, ensure learning and belonging, and support reintegration back to the classroom. Today, there are over 3,500 active AV1 robots used across 18 European countries. Positioned in the EdTech sector, AV1 is a unique solution to the growing issue of persistent absence, supporting both the academic and social needs of students. No Isolation works across Europe, with 45 employees across Europe and in offices in Oslo, Munich and London. Join us in our growth journey!

jobs.title: Computational Designer - Architecture & AI
jobs.description:
Our mission is to help architects bring their vision to life. We’re building a web-based application for architects that speed up their design workflows and makes high-quality visualization accessible to a wider audience.

We have experienced rapid growth in recent months and we are hiring to further scale the company. We have customers in over 120 different countries, including leading offices such as Nordic, Leo A Daly, and S+A, who collectively have generated over 6 million visualizations on our platform since the company was established in 2023.

We’ve raised over €3 million from leading Nordic investors to date, helping us build toward our mission. We’re now looking for talented individuals who want to challenge the status quo and reinvent how architects and industry professionals communicate their designs.

 

What you will do

As we are developing a professional tool for architects, industry knowledge is central to creating the best experience for our users at Visoid.

As our internal architect, you will work as a core part of the Product Team. Your role is to translate industry challenges and opportunities for the product team, be an internal power user for developing and testing solutions, and actively explore workflows to solve those challenges.

If you enjoy and have experience building technical solutions to optimize the architectural design process, we would love to hear from you.

In this role you will:

  • Explore and test technical solutions and workflows to solve industry challenges, including the latest AI models and parametric design workflows.

  • Be the internal voice of the industry, helping to translate industry challenges to product designers and engineers.

  • Prioritize which challenges to solve to help Visoid move forward.

  • Test developed solutions to ensure they meet user requirements.

 

Who you are

We are seeking a creative individual with a commercial mindset who is as obsessed with our users as we are. You should be a self-motivated team player committed to delivering real value and solving genuine user problems.

We think you will thrive in Visoid if:

  • You have an ability to communicate with users and apply insights into concrete product improvements.

  • You have a startup mindset and can independently prioritize the most valuable tasks when resources are limited.

  • You are self-driven with a “doer” mentality focused on moving fast and getting the job done.

  • You are eager to learn and acquire new skills.

 

Minimum Requirements

  • At least a Bachelor level degree in Architecture.

  • At least 5 years of experience with architectural design and/or Computational Design in a leading international architectural firm.

  • Proven architectural skills and deep interest for architecture.

  • Professional experience working with the technical side of generative AI - such as experimenting with generative image models, building ComfyUI workflows, training LoRAs for professional use cases.

  • Familiarity with multiple BIM, 3D modeling, and architectural visualization software such as Archicad, Revit, 3ds Max, and Enscape.

  • Professional experience in building tools for design workflows in applications such as Grasshopper.

  • Adaptable and comfortable working in a growing startup environment with shifting priorities in a fast-paced environment.

  • Strong collaboration skills and interest in working cross-functionally with sales, product, and content teams.

 

Optional qualifications

  • Worked at a software company in the AEC space.

  • Worked as a Product Manager or Product Designer.

  • Familiar with developing apps with the support of agents.

  • Already built software solutions for the AEC space.

We are looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The optional qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

We prioritize candidates that are either are already located in Oslo, or who have an existing right to work in Norway and are willing to relocate to Oslo.

 

Perks and benefits

We strive to offer competitive benefits for our employees. Here's what you can expect from us:

  • 4% pension contribution

  • Flexible work hours

  • Flexible home-office arrangement

  • 5 weeks vacation

  • Choice of computer equipment and mobile device

  • Gym membership

  • Cantina with subsidized lunch

  • Monthly social and educational events

     

We are located at StartupLab, the leading co-working space for startups in Norway.

 

Compensation and equity

We offer a competitive salary, adjusted for early-stage growth companies.

As an early hire you have the unique opportunity to secure a significant equity stake in the company. You will be directly invested in our success and share the rewards as we grow. Your contributions will not only shape the future of the company but also provide you with substantial financial upside if we achieve our goals.

 

About the team

As a company, we foster a team-focused culture that values ambition, collaboration and honesty. We want to assemble a team of innovative technologists and product enthusiasts who are passionate about building a great product for our users.

With the company numbering 12 employees, and already representing 10 different nationalities, we are no doubt a diverse group of people. Most of us are located in-person at the Oslo office in Norway.

 

Working at Visoid

We believe in a high-performance culture driven by speed, user impact, and continuous improvement through direct, respectful feedback. We favor rapid iteration and a "move fast and learn" approach over perfection. If you thrive in a dynamic environment, want to directly impact the product, and aren't afraid to challenge the status quo, you'll fit right in.

Beyond the work, we value a positive, inclusive atmosphere. To stay motivated, creative, and connected, we host monthly team social events where we try out new activities and simply enjoy spending time together.

 

Why Norway?

Norway combines a thriving tech industry with high living standards, and strong social benefits. Since English is widely spoken, international talent can easily settle in and feel at home.

Oslo itself is uniquely positioned: local public transport can take you to both the sea and the mountains in under 30 minutes. Whether you’re an outdoor enthusiast, an urban explorer, or a foodie looking to enjoy the city's rich restaurant and museum scene, Oslo truly has something for everyone.

jobs.title: Creative & AI Producer – 20–40% Student Position
jobs.description:
Creative & AI Producer – 20–40% Student Position

We have a slightly unusual setup.

We run several businesses and projects across hospitality, consumer products, media and design. Some are established businesses with employees, customers and real revenue. Others are early-stage ideas we are trying to turn into something real.

Møllefossen is a café, event venue and hospitality concept in Oslo. We are building a premium Norwegian mineral water brand, work with wine import, develop consumer products and are launching a podcast about what it is actually like to own and run a business in Norway.

More ideas tend to appear faster than we can execute them.

That is where you come in.

We are looking for a talented student who can help us turn ideas into things people can actually see, watch, visit, buy and experience.

This is not a traditional marketing position. There will be very few PowerPoints about what we could do. We would much rather make it, put it live, see if it works and improve it.

What you might actually do

One week you could be:

  • Building a landing page for a new concept

  • Filming a podcast and turning 90 minutes into great Reels and Shorts

  • Developing packaging or visual concepts for a new product

  • Creating content for Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn or YouTube

  • Improving one of our websites

  • Shooting photo and video

  • Making graphics and campaign material

  • Using AI to prototype a new brand or idea in an afternoon

  • Automating something we currently waste far too much time doing

The next week could be completely different.

AI should be part of how you work

We think AI is fundamentally changing what a small, talented team can accomplish. We already use it extensively, and we want you to push this much further.

ChatGPT, Claude, Midjourney, Runway, Framer, Lovable, Cursor – or something that launches next month. We don’t particularly care which tools you prefer.

We care about what you can make with them.

We are not looking for endless mediocre AI content. Taste still matters. Probably more than ever.

The goal is to combine good ideas, visual judgement and technology to move much faster from:

“We should do this” → “It’s live.”

Who we’re looking for

You might study design, marketing, communication, media, technology – or something completely different. Your degree matters less to us than how you think and what you can create.

You probably:

  • Have a very good visual eye

  • Are unusually comfortable with technology

  • Experiment with AI

  • Know some combination of Figma, Adobe, Canva, CapCut, Premiere, DaVinci, Webflow, Framer or similar

  • Can shoot decent photo and video

  • Learn new tools quickly

  • Take initiative

  • Actually enjoy figuring things out

You don’t need to know everything. We’d rather hire someone who knows 50% and learns incredibly fast than someone who ticks every box but lacks curiosity.

What the job is like

You will work directly with the people building the businesses. Short decision paths, very little bureaucracy and plenty of room to influence the result.

Have a better idea? Tell us. Find a tool that does in 30 minutes what we spend a day doing? Use it. Something isn’t working? Change it.

The role is 20–40%, with flexibility around studies and exams. Some work can be remote, while filming, photography and certain projects require you to be with us in Oslo/Bærum.

It’s an unusual student job where you can build a portfolio of real work across several businesses instead of spending a year making minor adjustments to one company’s social media calendar.

How to apply

Don’t spend an evening writing a polished cover letter.

Send us:

  • A short introduction

  • Three things you’ve made that you’re genuinely proud of

Website, video, design, Instagram account, school project, side project, app, brand, photography – whatever shows us what you can do.

A CV is welcome, but isn’t the most important part.

Show us what you can make.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Jeg ville ikke prøvd å beskrive dere som én startup med én problemstilling. Det interessante er nettopp at kandidaten kommer inn i et lite økosystem av ekte virksomheter og nye konsepter. På The Hub er det en styrke, særlig for den typen tech/AI-nysgjerrige student vi vil ha. Jeg ville skrevet det slik: About us We have a slightly unusual setup. We run several businesses and projects across hospitality, consumer products, media and design. Some are established businesses with employees, customers and real revenue. Others are early-stage ideas we are currently trying to turn into something real. Møllefossen is a café, event venue and hospitality concept in Oslo. We are building a premium Norwegian mineral water brand. We work with wine import, are developing new consumer products, and are currently launching a podcast. More ideas tend to appear faster than we can execute them. That is essentially the problem we are trying to solve. We are good at coming up with concepts, building businesses, finding opportunities and getting things moving. But today, a surprisingly large part of turning an idea into reality is digital: a website needs to be built, a brand needs an identity, something needs to be filmed, a product needs packaging, a podcast needs to become 15 good clips, or an idea needs to be tested before spending weeks and a lot of money on it. AI is changing how much a very small team can actually do. We want to take advantage of that properly – not by generating endless mediocre content, but by combining good taste, creativity and new technology to move much faster from “we should do this” to “it’s live.” That is why we are looking for someone who gets genuinely excited by having Framer open in one window, ChatGPT or Claude in another, a half-finished Reel on the screen and a completely new project landing on their desk the following week. If you need a clearly defined corporate job description and six months of planning before launching something, this probably isn’t the right place. If that sounds like fun, it might be.

jobs.title: Utviklere til Labrador CMS
jobs.description:
Hvem er vi?

Labrador CMS er en norsk publiseringsplattform for nettaviser bygget av journalister og utviklere. Plattformen brukes av ti tusen journalister i hundrevis av nettaviser i 20 land i Europa, Asia og USA. 

Nå søker vi tre nye  utviklere (backend/frontend/fullstack) som vil være med på å videreutvikle produktet, kundeoppsett og brukeropplevelser for redaksjoner og lesere. Dette er roller for deg som trives i skjæringspunktet mellom produkt, teknologi og praktiske kundebehov. Vi er opptatt av å være til å stole på og samtidig være tidlig ute med ny teknologi. Vi trenger folk som både kan kode manuelt samt orkestrere kodeagenter og agentsystemer. Hos oss kan du i stor grad påvirke verktøykassen selv. Du kan bruke Claude Code eller Codex, Mac, Windows eller Linux. Du bør like å tenke stort og langt og være ambisiøs. Vi liker folk som både klarer å finne ut hvor vi bør bli bedre og i tillegg foreslår løsningen og løser problemet.


Roller og ansvarsområder

Avhengig av kompetanse og interesse er det flere områder du kan jobbe i hos oss:

Import/onboarding-team

Når nye kunder går over til Labrador CMS, skal nettstedene deres settes opp på en måte som er stabil, effektiv og enkel å videreutvikle. Rollen innebærer å konfigurere og tilpasse løsninger, bygge eller koble på integrasjoner mot blant annet betalingsmurer, kommentarsystemer og printsystemer, og samtidig bidra til at hovedproduktet blir bedre for alle kunder. Vi importerer også alle eksisterende artikler, så gjennomføring av dette samt videreutvikling av verktøyene vi bruker kan også være del av jobben.

Produkt-team

Denne rollen handler både om presentasjonen ut mot leserne og arbeidsflyten inne i redaksjonen. Du er med på å bygge raske, gjennomarbeidede og visuelt sterke forsider og artikkelsider for kundene våre.

Samtidig skal du bidra til å forenkle brukergrensesnittet og arbeidsflyten i editoren i Labrador CMS. Dette er en hands-on utviklerrolle, der du både vurderer løsningene og bygger dem selv. Rollen kan også innebære dialog med kunder, slik at tekniske valg forankres i faktiske behov.


Om Labrador CMS

Labrador CMS leverer en skybasert publiseringsplattform for mediebransjen. Plattformen er egenutviklet fra bunnen av for å gi redaksjoner rask, sikker og brukervennlig publisering. Mange kunder bruker Labrador som en komplett løsning, mens større mediehus bygger videre på plattformen sammen med egne utviklere.

Vi leverer også frontend-hosting for kundene våre og håndterer høy trafikk på tvers av mange nettsteder. Oppetid, responstid og stabile leveranser er derfor en naturlig del av hverdagen hos oss.

Arbeidsform og team

Labrador har rundt 40 ansatte, hovedsakelig i Norge. Over halvparten jobber med utvikling, fordelt på frontend, backend og infrastruktur. Hovedkontoret ligger i Oslo, men vi har også ansatte andre steder i landet. Det er mulig å jobbe remote, samtidig som vi verdsetter tett samarbeid og korte veier fra idé til løsning.


Vi tilbyr

  • Mulighet til å påvirke et produkt som brukes av redaksjoner og lesere i mange land

  • Et sterkt utviklingsmiljø med høy faglig takhøyde og korte beslutningsveier

  • Fleksibel arbeidshverdag, med moderne lokaler hos MESH sentralt i Oslo

  • Konkurransedyktige betingelser og fritt valg av arbeidsutstyr.


Hvem er du?

  • Du kommuniserer godt på norsk og engelsk

  • Du jobber strukturert og leverer riktig kvalitet til riktig tid

  • Du er produktnær, hands-on og opptatt av både visuell kvalitet og gode arbeidsflyter

  • Du har relevant utdanning eller erfaring som gir deg et godt teknisk fundament

  • Erfaring med integrasjoner, frontend, backend eller systemer med høye krav til oppetid og tilgjengelighet er en fordel


Teknologier vi bruker:

(du trenger ikke kunne alt dette)

  • Codex og Claude Code

  • Git

  • HTML/CSS

  • JavaScript

  • Go

  • PHP

  • PostgreSQL

  • OpenSearch

  • AWS

Nysgjerrig? Send inn søknad på linken med CV vedlagt. Søknadsfrist: snarest.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Built in Norway by journalists and developers who understand what deadline-driven publishing actually demands, Labrador CMS has grown into one of the fastest-growing publishing platforms in the world. Today, 10,000 journalists produce content for 400 online newspapers across 21 countries on Labrador — and the platform serves the 4 billion monthly page views their audiences generate. Over the past year, some of Europe's largest media groups have made Labrador their platform of choice. We're also seeing strong momentum in the US and Asia. Our customers range from major national newspapers and large regional publishing groups to magazines and niche digital outlets. Labrador is known for being highly flexible, genuinely easy to use, and for shipping market-leading AI features that help editorial teams work faster and smarter. We believe the future of publishing is one where AI agents work alongside journalists — and we're building for that future now. When employees tell what they like most about working for Labrador CMS, they speak about how inspiring it is to see their work be used in production for thousands of users and read by millions of people. They also talk about our culture for collaboration. We work hard and we acheive results, and we help each other to reach our potential.

jobs.title: AV Scriptwriter
jobs.description:
At Superside, we're looking for an AV Scriptwriter who can take a video brief from the initial idea through to a production-ready script. Projects range from 15-second social and performance content to five-minute brand/explainer films, across motion graphics, live action, stock-led video, and UGC. You'll need to understand how words, visuals, pacing, and sound work together, and be confident writing dialogue, voiceover, and on-screen copy that reads naturally out loud.


What you’ll do

  • Concept and script AV content across formats, from short-form social cuts to longer branded films.

  • Given a brief, develop two or three distinct creative directions, each with a clear sense of how it would work as a video, supported by references and a potential title approach.

jobs.title: Lead Product Designer (UX/UI)
jobs.description:
About Six Robotics

At Six Robotics, we build intelligent software that gives Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) the ability to collaborate, adapt on the fly, and execute missions that were previously impossible.

From our base in Oslo, our team of 90+ engineers, researchers, and defence specialists develops our autonomy and swarm platform, used by both government and industry. Working closely with the Norwegian Defence Research Establishment (FFI) and end users, we move quickly from ideas to field deployment, solving problems where software meets the real world.

The challenges we work on don’t come with existing playbooks. They demand deep technical thinking, close collaboration across disciplines, and the ability to learn quickly as both the technology and the company evolve.

At Six Robotics, every person executes with precision, adapts to changing conditions, and strengthens the team. If you’re excited about building systems that matter and growing alongside talented people that push boundaries every day, you’ll find no better place to deliver real-world impact.

About The Role

We're looking for a Lead Product Designer to design the interface operators use to control Valkyrie — the screens, workflows, and interactions that let them command autonomous assets in the field. You'll be designing for real-time control, situational awareness, and operational trust in environments where clarity, speed, and precision aren't "nice to have" — they're the entire point.

This is a hands-on role. You'll own the design process from concept to implementation, while also starting to build and lead a small (but growing) design team. We're looking for someone who's just as comfortable designing themselves as they are showing others the way.

You'll help shape a product domain from an early stage, with real influence over how operators in the field actually experience and trust the technology they use. We move fast and keep bureaucracy out of the way.

What You Will Do

- Lead design for key GCS (Ground Control Station) capabilities, from early concept through launch

- Own product feature design end to end — from problem framing to shipped, polished UI

- Work closely with engineers, autonomy teams, product, and operators to translate technical and operational requirements into intuitive workflows

- Drive research efforts and generate insight that shapes what we build — talking to operators, testing assumptions, and turning findings into design direction

- Drive the end-to-end design process — wireframes, prototypes, detailed UI specs, and implementation support

- Test and iterate with real users, building feedback into the process continuously

- Lead our design system components, and define and maintain a coherent visual and interaction language that supports real-time control and situational awareness

- Ensure high quality in the final product — sweating the details that make the difference between "usable" and "trusted in the field"

- Solve unsolved problems: tackle complex challenges where there's no existing playbook. Think pragmatically and creatively to design interfaces for remote hardware sensing, 3D spatial awareness, and AI-driven missions

- Start building a design team: setting direction, mentoring, and eventually taking on people leadership as the team grows

- Contribute to roadmap prioritization and product vision across the GCS domain

- Travel to test flights and field operations to drive operator research where it actually happens

What we are looking for

- Minimum 8+ years experience as a product designer (UX/UI), with a proven track record of leading complex product areas end to end

- Have a strong visual design sensibility - you care about craft and polish - paired with real UX depth: you think in flows, systems, and user problems, not just screens

- Have formal training or professional experience in complex systems, with a portfolio that shows deep, pragmatic thinking - not just polished visuals

- Have experience designing for complex, interactive systems - ideally involving spatial data, control interfaces, or high information density

- Have B2B experience and a pragmatic approach to product development

- Have experience leading or mentoring other designers, or are ready to take that step

- Communicate well across disciplines — you can explain design decisions and tradeoffs to people who aren't designers

- Are comfortable with ambiguity and have a bias for action in a fast-moving environment

- Want to build something from the ground up, not just polish what already exists

Nice to have

- Experience designing interfaces for real-time control systems (drones, robotics, vehicles, or aviation platforms)

- Familiarity with defence, intelligence, or mission-critical systems

- Experience with 2D/3D map visualization, telemetry, or command-and-control interfaces

- Background in early-stage product development or entrepreneurial environments

Why You Should Join

  • Build at the edge of what’s possible: You’ll work on problems the industry hasn’t solved yet, alongside people who are pushing the boundaries of autonomy, AI, and robotics.

  • Grow as fast as the company: We believe that chance favours those in motion. The role you’re hired into is just the starting point. As Six Robotics evolves, so will your scope, your responsibilities, and your opportunities.

  • Work with exceptional people: Surround yourself with people who raise your own standards. You’ll join a team of ambitious engineers and operators who care deeply about the quality of their work. Expectations are high, but so is the willingness to help each other improve.

  • Ship work that matters. The things you build don't stay in a demo environment. They get deployed, tested, and used where reliability and performance genuinely matter.

  • Supported by great benefits. Alongside meaningful work, we offer competitive compensation, equity potential, strong pension and insurance plans, gadget budgets, modern equipment, panoramic offices, and the flexibility you need to do your best work.

Our Recruitment Process

We want hiring to be transparent and respectful of your time. We aim to move with momentum while making thoughtful hiring decisions - because every new team member matters.

Our process typically includes:

  • Initial phone screening (30 min): A conversation about your background, motivation, and the role.

  • First interview (45 min): Meet the hiring team, learn more about Six Robotics, and discuss your experience.

  • Second interview (60–90 min): A technical discussion, typically including a live case presentation.

  • Final interview (45 min): Meet members of our leadership team to align expectations and answer any remaining questions.

Reference checks are conducted before an offer is finalized. We review applications continuously, so don't leave us hanging. Send us your application today!

Our Commitment to Inclusion

At Six Robotics, we are committed to creating a workplace built on respect, integrity, and collaboration. We value different perspectives and experiences, and we believe that diversity within our team strengthens both our work and our culture. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply and help us build technology that makes a real impact.

Security Clearance Requirement

All employees at Six Robotics must be eligible for security clearance. Some roles might require a high level of clearance, depending on the nature of the work. If you are hired, we’ll guide you through any required authorization or clearance process as part of your onboarding. Previous authorization or clearance is not required, but all candidates must be eligible to obtain the necessary approvals if required for their role.

jobs.title: Business Systems Lead
jobs.description:
About Monil

Monil develops technology that is transforming how livestock is managed.

Our platform combines virtual fencing, GPS tracking and animal intelligence to help farmers monitor animal health, automate grazing and gain deeper insight into their herds. Our ambition is to become the leading digital platform for livestock management.

Founded in Norway in 2022, Monil has grown rapidly into an international technology company with more than 60 employees across Norway, Sweden, the UK and the US. We are now entering our next phase of growth, with plans to expand into new markets and continue rapid scaling internationally.

Today, more than 3,000 customers use Monil to manage their animals every day. As we continue expanding internationally, building scalable internal systems is becoming just as important as building great products.

Why we're hiring

As Monil grows, the complexity of our business grows with it.

New markets, new products, new legal entities and increasing transaction volumes place higher demands on our business systems, data and processes.

We're looking for a Business Systems Lead who will own and continuously improve the systems that enable Monil to scale efficiently.

Working across Commercial, Operations, Product and Finance, you'll simplify business processes, improve data quality and ensure our business systems evolve alongside the company.

Your mission

Your mission is simple:

Make Monil easier to scale.

You will ensure that our business systems become an increasingly powerful competitive advantage by improving processes, strengthening data quality and reducing manual work.

You will combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution and work closely with both internal stakeholders and external partners to deliver solutions that create measurable business value.

What you'll ownBusiness Systems

  • Own and continuously improve our ERP system (Odoo) as Monil's core business platform.

  • Prioritise the business system roadmap together with stakeholders across the company.

  • Ensure that our business systems support scalable ways of working, rather than local workarounds.

Business Process Improvement

  • Own the high-level overview of how business processes and systems connect across Monil.

  • Ensure systems, data flows and workflows are integrated and scalable.

  • Identify cross-functional gaps, bottlenecks and unnecessary manual work, and coordinate improvements with the relevant process owners.

  • Drive standardisation where it creates value, while ensuring individual teams retain ownership of their functional processes.

System Architecture & Integrations

  • Define how Monil's business systems work together.

  • Design scalable integrations between ERP, CRM, product platforms, payment providers, logistics and other core applications.

  • Improve data quality, master data governance, and system ownership.

Automation & AI

  • Identify opportunities to automate repetitive work.

  • Introduce AI-enabled workflows where they create measurable business value.

  • Continuously evaluate new technologies that improve productivity or decision making.

Vendors & Governance

  • Manage external implementation partners and business system vendors.

  • Help prioritise investments based on business value, complexity and long-term maintainability.

  • Own access management and establish lightweight governance for business systems, data ownership and change management.

What success looks like

Within your first 12–24 months you have:

  • Established the ERP as the operational backbone of Monil.

  • Standardised and simplified our most important business processes.

  • Built reliable integrations between our core business systems.

  • Improved data quality and established clear ownership of master data.

  • Created a scalable business systems platform that supports continued international growth.

We're probably a good match if you

  • Have led implementation or significant development of an ERP or other core business platform.

  • Enjoy improving business processes through technology.

  • Have experience working with integrations between business-critical systems.

  • Understand how Commercial, Operations, Product and Finance teams work together.

  • Are comfortable moving between strategy, prioritisation and hands-on execution.

  • Prefer solving business problems over implementing technology for its own sake.

Experience with Odoo, APIs, process automation or AI tools is an advantage, but not a requirement.

Who you are

You're someone who naturally looks for a better way of doing things and makes sure it gets done.

You enjoy understanding how businesses operate and translating that understanding into better systems and simpler processes.

You are analytical without overcomplicating things, pragmatic without compromising quality, and comfortable taking ownership in a fast-growing organisation.

Most importantly, you care about creating solutions that people actually use.

Why this role?

Few companies have the opportunity to build their internal operating platform from an early stage while scaling internationally.

You'll have significant influence over how Monil operates for years to come, working directly with senior leadership and stakeholders across the business.

Rather than maintaining existing systems, you'll help design the processes, architecture and business platform that support the company's next phase of growth.

If you enjoy solving complex business problems through systems, data and automation, you'll find plenty to build at Monil.

This role is based at our HQ at Lysaker and reports to the CFO.

Please upload your CV and a short application describing a relevant ERP or business system implementation, clearly outlining your personal responsibilities, ownership and contribution to the process.

jobs.description:
Build something monumental for Healthcare!

At Tandem Health we’re reimagining healthcare by putting clinicians first. Our platform - designed by clinicians, for clinicians - is built on deep insight into real-world pain points, with intuitive medical notes and workflows that truly support patient care.

We’re a fast-scaling health-tech company backed by top investors and expanding globally. We move fast, stay curious, and believe building something that matters starts with an extraordinary team. If you're passionate about impact and innovation, we'd love to meet you!

About the Role

We’re looking for a Senior Account Executive to drive and expand Tandem’s footprint across Norway. In this role, you will lead sales processes, with a particular focus on the private healthcare market, and build strategic partnerships with our commercial partners.

You will navigate complex buying environments involving multiple stakeholders across clinical, operational, IT, and executive teams. This role requires strong commercial experience with the ability to position Tandem as a trusted partner in healthcare transformation.

What You Will Do

  • Lead complex sales cycles from outbound sales motions through to negotiation, and close.

  • Manage multi-stakeholder relationships across clinical, operational, IT, and executive functions.

  • Develop strategic account plans to grow Tandem’s presence across the Norwegian healthcare market.

  • Build long-term relationships with healthcare professionals, decision-makers, and commercial partners across the private healthcare market.

  • Act as a trusted advisor by understanding customer workflows, operational challenges, and organisational priorities.

  • Drive both direct sales and partner-led commercial initiatives in collaboration with strategic partners.

  • Represent Tandem Health at conferences, trade fairs, and industry events.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Medical Operations, Product, Marketing, and Leadership teams to continuously improve our offering and customer experience.

  • Maintain strong pipeline management and forecasting discipline using CRM and modern GTM tools.

What You Bring

  • Proven experience in sales, ideally within SaaS and healthcare technology.

  • Strong track record managing complex sales cycles with multiple stakeholders.

  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and presentation skills across both clinical and commercial audiences.

  • Strategic, structured, and proactive approach to sales and account management.

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

  • Native-level Norwegian and fluent English.

  • Passion for improving healthcare delivery through impactful technology.

  • Genuine passion for technology and AI - deep technical expertise is not required, but curiosity and enthusiasm are essential qualities we seek.

Bonus Points

  • Experience selling into EHR providers, health systems, or healthcare organisations.

  • Background in health tech, digital health, or regulated software.

  • Experience working in startup or scale-up environments.

  • Degree in business, healthcare management, or a related field.

How to Apply

We adopt a continuous selection process, so please make sure to apply with your CV in English.

Our interview process consists of stages:

  1. Screening interview with Talent Acquisition

  2. First interview with Norway Country Lead

  3. Second interview Head of Commercial Excellence

  4. Third interview with our Country Director

  5. Working Day - Join us in the Stockholm office for a day to experience our culture firsthand, collaborate with our team, and see how you work in action.

     
Culture at Tandem

At Tandem, we move fast, think big, and take ownership. We're a high-performing, diverse team with a shared drive to change the future of healthcare - and we’re just getting started.

Our culture is built on action, ambition, and learning. You'll be trusted to take the lead, challenge yourself, and make an impact from day one. We believe real growth happens when you're stretched, supported, and surrounded by smart, passionate teammates who want to win together.

Even though we’re spread across countries, we come together often in Sweden for team meetings, social events, and offsites - blending global reach with real human connection.

We hire for talent, potential, and attitude - valuing different backgrounds and fresh perspectives. Great ideas come from everywhere, and we’re building a team that reflects the world we want to change.

Tandem handles sensitive patient data and will conduct a background check before hiring any candidate.
